summary:
Our project is called "Forgotten Giants." This name was chosen to highlight the importance of the equipment that has been sent into space over the years. It addresses the challenge "Abandoned but Not Forgotten" through an interactive website primarily designed for children and teenagers aged 6 to 15.

We believe that access to reliable, official, and well-supported information is essential so that those interested in this topic can conduct in-depth research and perhaps develop innovative projects that could contribute to the world. Although the platform may also be interesting to people of any age, we recognize that students at higher educational levels usually conduct research using other types of more formal sources, such as scientific publications and academic articles.

The website features a model of the Solar System that allows users to select different spacecraft, probes, or a space telescope, as well as the Moon and Mars. Users can explore a 3D view of their surfaces, where additional hardware used in NASA missions can be found.

The platform provides relevant information about each object, including its location, dates, and current status. It also features a timeline slider that allows users to select a specific year. If a piece of equipment had not yet been launched or did not yet exist during the selected year, it will no longer be highlighted.
details:
Our website allows users to explore and learn about different pieces of equipment and spacecraft launched by NASA into space or sent to specific destinations, such as the Moon and Mars.

It combines written information with interactive 3D models, allowing visitors to visualize the equipment while learning about its purpose, historical background, launch dates, and missions. Users can also explore orbital animations and interact with the visualization to better understand the context of these missions. Additionally, the platform supports the implementation of GLB files, allowing users to incorporate and explore their own 3D models.

Our project also makes learning about space exploration more accessible, engaging, and interactive, especially for students and space enthusiasts.

By combining constantly moving orbital animations, attractive 3D models, and organized written information, the website captures users' attention and encourages them to explore the content in greater depth. Instead of simply reading historical information, visitors can visually interact with the subject, making complex topics easier to understand and remember.

It also encourages interest in science, technology, engineering, and 3D modeling.

Our main goal is to encourage people to access reliable information and understand the importance of NASA's space missions.

We want users to discover how space exploration has evolved over the years, how the technology and hardware used in different missions have changed, and how these achievements are connected through historical dates and chronological events.

We also aim to create a useful educational resource for students, researchers, and space enthusiasts. Beyond providing information, our platform encourages creativity and technological exploration by allowing users to incorporate GLB files, promoting 3D modeling, rendering, and visualization as tools for learning about space.

We used a combination of web development technologies, programming languages, 3D modeling software, and visualization libraries to develop our project:

  • HTML: Used to structure the website and organize its content and interactive elements.
  • CSS: Used to design the website's interface, visual appearance, animations, and responsive layout.
  • JavaScript: Used to program the website's interactive features, navigation, orbital visualizations, and 3D interactions.
  • Three.js: A JavaScript library used to render and display interactive 3D environments and models directly in the browser.
  • Python: Used to automate the creation of 3D environments and animations through Blender's Python API.
  • Blender: Used for 3D modeling, scene development, and procedural environment generation. We created a solar system with animated orbital movements, as well as lunar and Martian landscapes featuring craters, rocky terrain, procedural materials, lighting, and reference points for spacecraft and exploration missions.
  • GLB / GLTF: 3D model formats used to integrate spacecraft, rovers, and other objects into our website through Three.js and GLTFLoader.
  • BLEND: Blender project files used to save and organize our 3D scenes and their editable elements.
  • GitHub: Used to host and publish our website online.

The creativity of our project stands out through its combination of historical space exploration, interactive visualization, and 3D technology.

Instead of presenting information through traditional text and static images, we created an interactive solar system where users can explore different destinations, discover historical missions, follow orbital animations, and visualize the equipment left behind in space.

Another creative aspect is the ability to upload and display custom GLB files, allowing users to experiment with their own 3D models. This transforms the website from a simple educational resource into an interactive environment that encourages creativity, technological experimentation, and a deeper interest in space exploration.

Our main creative idea is to bring forgotten space missions back into people's attention through a visual and immersive experience.

During the development of our project, we considered several important factors:

  1. Educational value: The information should be understandable and useful for students, researchers, and space enthusiasts.
  2. Historical accuracy: We aimed to organize mission information chronologically and use reliable sources, particularly NASA's NSSDCA catalog.
  3. User experience: The interface needed to be visually appealing, intuitive, and easy to navigate.
  4. Accessibility: We wanted users to access the information directly through a website without needing to install additional software.
  5. Performance: We considered the need to display 3D models and orbital animations while maintaining a smooth browsing experience.
  6. Creativity and participation: We incorporated GLB file support to encourage users to experiment with 3D modeling and contribute to the exploration experience.
  7. Scientific relevance: We wanted to highlight the historical and technological importance of space missions, including equipment that remains in space or on other celestial bodies.

All these factors helped us shape a project that combines scientific information, technology, and interactive learning.
